findings.summary: Non-blocking: the entry script never records the production bus (7490) head_seq, so the run record it generates lacks the pre/post readings that acceptance criterion 8 asks the implementer to leave behind in support of Z2. The substantive Z2 property still holds by construction (defaults target 7495 and the guard refuses any 7490/production-token configuration, as T-C proves with a zero-request counting bus), and Z1-Z3 are dispatcher-executed host verifications, so this only costs the host verifier the convenience of in-record readings rather than invalidating the criterion.

Non-blocking: two EXIT traps are registered back to back, but bash replaces a signal's handler instead of stacking it, so 'rm -f "$ENTRY_TMP"' is discarded and only _persist_record ever runs. The mktemp buffer therefore leaks one small file into /tmp per invocation, and the comment on the preceding line asserting LIFO ordering ('persist first, rm second') is factually wrong, as is the claim at :52 that the buffer is cleaned up on the guard-rejection path. No repo pollution results, so the §2.3.5 prohibition is still met and record archival works.

Non-blocking observation on inherited behavior: the entry script delegates terminal-state judgment entirely to the inner chain, and check-drain-failures.mjs exits 0 when drain output is empty, unparseable, or missing drain_id. The specific G11 zero-spawn case named by §2.3.6 is covered by the laneEntries.length === 0 branch, but a drain that emits no parseable JSON would still surface as exit 0 with no independent assertion of terminal state by the entry layer. Hardening this belongs to the E7 rewrite that §4 explicitly places out of scope for this package.
